title: How You're Losing Up to 20% of Your Pipeline After Hours
summary: B2B teams lose up to 20% of their pipeline to leads that arrive after hours. Calculate how much yours loses while it is offline, with your own numbers.
body_markdown:
Short answer


1 in 3 B2B buyers want to see a product outside office hours, and 1 in 10 on a weekend. When nobody is there to give them a demo, they book one about 31% less often (29% against 42%), according to a survey of 28 B2B companies in travel, HR and fintech with at least $50M in ARR. Depending on how many of your leads arrive after hours, that costs you between 10% and 20% of your pipeline.


## How much pipeline do you lose after hours?


Put in your own numbers. The example uses 400 demo requests a month, a third of them after hours and a $15,000 ACV (average contract value per year).


Pipeline you lose after hours, every year


$2.8M


in demos never booked because nobody was there to give them


**10%** of your potential pipeline


**186** missed demos a year


**$1.1M** in deals you would have won


For every *10* demos you could book, *1* never happens because the buyer asked when your team was offline.


### How the calculator works


It starts from one gap. In a survey of 28 B2B companies in travel, HR and fintech with at least $50M in ARR, **29%** of the leads that arrived after hours booked a demo, against **42%** of the leads that arrived during office hours. After-hours leads booked about 31% less often. The calculator applies that gap to your numbers in three steps:


1. It splits the booking rate you entered into two: an office-hours rate and an after-hours rate 31% lower, so that together they average to your rate.
2. It counts how many more after-hours requests would book a demo at the office-hours rate. Those are your missed demos.
3. Missed demos times your ACV is the pipeline you lose. Multiply that by your win rate and you get the deals you would have won.


With the default numbers, the 34% booking rate splits into 38% during office hours and 26% after hours. That gap, on the 132 requests a month that arrive after hours, is about 15 missed demos a month. The share of your potential pipeline you lose is your after-hours share times 31%: about 10% when 1 in 3 leads arrive after hours, and 19% at 61%, the share the survey companies saw when they also counted early mornings and Friday afternoons as after hours.


The rest of this post shows when B2B buyers ask to see a product, how serious they are when they do it after hours, and how to stop losing them. The data comes from the demos Karumi's AI agents run every day.


## When do B2B buyers ask for a demo?


We looked at every demo our[AI demo agents](https://karumi.ai/blog/what-is-an-ai-demo-agent) gave in production, by the buyer's local time. **1 in 3 happened outside 9am to 6pm on a weekday** : in the evening, early in the morning or on the weekend. 1 in 10 happened on a Saturday or a Sunday.

Demand peaks late in the morning and stays high until the end of the afternoon. It does not stop at 6pm: between 6pm and midnight buyers still take about 1 in 6 demos. That is the time many of them finally have to look at a new tool without meetings in the way.


## Are after-hours buyers less serious?


A common objection is that people who browse at night are curious and not ready to buy. Our production data says otherwise. During after-hours demos, **12.1%** of buyers asked about pricing or about talking to sales. During office hours the figure is **12.7%** . Buyers show almost the same intent at 10pm as at 10am. What changes is whether someone is there to answer them.


## Why do after-hours leads book fewer demos?


- **The reply comes too late.** A buyer who asks on Friday at 5pm and hears back on Monday has spent the weekend on other things. This is what sales teams call **speed to lead** : the time between a request and the first useful answer.
- **A booking link only gives the buyer a date.** They still wait days for the call, and their interest has to survive the wait.
- **Other vendors are one tab away.** A buyer comparing tools at night spends time with whoever shows them something that night.


## How to stop losing demos after hours


Teams usually try one of three fixes. They cover different parts of the problem.

## FAQ


### What counts as after hours for B2B leads?


Any time your team cannot answer within minutes. The survey counted leads that arrived after 7pm, before 9:30am, on Friday from 3pm or on the weekend. Karumi's own demo data counts demos outside 9am to 6pm on weekdays, in the buyer's local time, plus weekends.


### What is speed to lead?


Speed to lead is the time between a buyer asking for something, such as a demo, and the first useful reply from the vendor. For leads that arrive after hours it is often measured in days.


### How do I calculate the pipeline I lose after hours?


Multiply the after-hours demos you do not book each year by your ACV. The calculator above does it with your demo requests, your after-hours share and your conversion rates.


### Does an AI demo agent replace my sales team?


No. It gives the first demo when the buyer asks, then hands interested buyers to your team with a record of what they asked and saw. Your team keeps the meetings that move the deal.
